title: A Silent Voice
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In elementary school, Shoya Ishida leads the bullying of Shoko Nishimiya, a deaf transfer student, until his classmates turn on him and he is isolated for years. As a suicidal high schooler he seeks her out to make amends, and the story follows both of them and their former classmates as they face guilt, depression and the hard work of reconciliation.
life_message: Holds up facing the harm you have done, making amends, and learning to forgive yourself and live with others.

content.note: Physical bullying of a deaf girl, hearing aids destroyed; Common Sense Media (film) and AniList Bullying 94% agree.
Emotional distress, a fall and a coma; no horror.
Occasional profanity in the film review (to verify for manga).
Wikipedia and the film review both describe a planned suicide and an attempt by jumping; depression and self-loathing run throughout.
Bullying tactics shown in detail but clearly condemned.

delivery.evidence: ANN's Nick Creamer calls it nuanced: themes come through everyday exchanges, not stated outright; bullies and teachers drawn as complex.

personified.ideology: facing past harm and making amends

delivery.note: Bullies, bystanders and teachers are shown with their own weaknesses, and redemption is slow and hard.

winners_losers: Shoya and Shoko both grow through accountability and friendship; cruelty and scapegoating are shown to harm everyone. Sympathy goes to the repentant and the excluded.
